name: Behavior-Driven Development
description: BDD — behavior-first design. Code structure follows user-observable behavior. Tests describe scenarios, not implementation details.

rules.name: Behavior-First Naming
rules.instruction: Name functions, methods, and types after what they do for the user, not how they do it internally. Prefer 'PlaceOrder' over 'InsertOrderRecord', 'AuthenticateUser' over 'CheckPasswordHash'.

rules.name: Given/When/Then Test Structure
rules.instruction: Tests follow Given (setup preconditions), When (execute the action), Then (assert the outcome). Each section is clearly delineated with comments or helper functions.

rules.name: Scenarios Describe Behavior
rules.instruction: Test names and descriptions use plain language describing observable behavior: 'user can check out with a valid coupon', not 'test_apply_discount_code_to_cart_total'. No implementation details in test names.

rules.name: One Behavior Per Test
rules.instruction: Each test verifies exactly one behavior or scenario. Multiple assertions are fine if they all verify the same behavior. Never test two independent behaviors in one function.

rules.name: Outside-In Design
rules.instruction: Design from the user's perspective inward. Start with the interface the user interacts with, then implement the layers that support it. The API shapes the internals, not the reverse.

rules.name: Feature Files or Scenario Docs
rules.instruction: For significant features, maintain a scenario document (markdown or .feature file) that describes acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then format. Code tests map to these scenarios.

rules.name: No Test Implementation Coupling
rules.instruction: Tests must not depend on internal implementation details (private fields, internal method call order, specific SQL queries). Test through the public API. If the implementation changes but behavior is preserved, tests must still pass.

rules.name: Readable Test Output
rules.instruction: Test failure messages must clearly state what behavior failed and what was expected. Use descriptive assertion messages, not bare 'got X, want Y'.

rules.name: Living Documentation
rules.instruction: Tests serve as documentation. A new developer should understand the system's behavior by reading the test suite. Organize tests by feature or user story, not by internal module.
